type.weight: font-medium for all display type and headings, font-semibold only for emphasis in running copy, never font-bold
type.rule: the hero headline is the largest type on the page

colour.rule: one accent colour on the primary CTA only, repeated at most once elsewhere; never place two recessed sections next to each other; every colour class needs its dark: counterpart

motion.stagger: delay: Math.min(index, 5) * 0.06, a section must finish revealing within 500ms
motion.reducedMotion: add useReducedMotion() and collapse to an opacity-only fade when it returns true

blocks.content: Product name, a mega-menu collapsed to the sections that actually exist, and one CTA matching the page-wide conversion label.

config.ctaLabel: match the page-wide CTA label verbatim
config.menus: keep only real product and solution links

blocks.fallback: A fixed 56-64px bar: product name left, up to four links, one primary action right.

blocks.content: Announcement pill with one real fact, a 4-8 word headline stating the one idea, a one-sentence subhead naming the audience, the primary CTA, and one real product visual.

config.actions: one primary CTA plus one text link
config.visual: real product screenshot or loop, never an illustration

blocks.fallback: A split hero: headline and subhead left, product screenshot right, single primary CTA.

blocks.content: Six recognisable customer logos under one line of trust copy. Remove this block entirely if the logos are not recognisable.
blocks.fallback: A single centered row of six grayscale logos under one caption line.

blocks.content: Three tabs, each naming a task the buyer does the hard way today and showing the product resolving it. This is the before/after narrative.

config.framing: buyer pain first, product answer second

blocks.fallback: Three stacked rows, each a pain statement paired with the product's answer and one visual.

blocks.content: Three to five capabilities as an icon grid. Outcome headline plus one sentence of mechanism each, ordered by buyer priority.

config.order: by buyer priority, not build effort

blocks.fallback: A responsive icon grid of three to five capability cards, one to three columns.

blocks.content: Three numbered steps from signup to first value, one visual per step. Step one must be honest about any card requirement.
blocks.fallback: Three numbered steps with a short caption and a supporting image each.

blocks.content: Three or four real value/label pairs with units. Remove this block if the numbers are not real.
blocks.fallback: A hairline-separated row of three animated numbers with captions.

blocks.content: Two to four quotes, each with a real name, role, and company, ideally about a specific outcome. Remove this block if quotes are not real.
blocks.fallback: A two-to-four card grid of quotes with attribution name, role, and company.

blocks.content: A feature checklist against the status quo the buyer actually weighs. Every row must be defensible.

config.against: the incumbent or manual process the buyer compares to

blocks.fallback: A two-column checklist table: product versus status quo, one row per capability.

blocks.content: Real prices and real limits with one highlighted plan, plus plain-text trial length, card requirement, and cancellation terms.
blocks.fallback: A hairline-separated pricing table stating each tier's binding limit and price.

blocks.content: Five to eight real objections including the card question, data handling, the comparison to the obvious alternative, contracts, and cancellation.
blocks.fallback: A keyboard-operable disclosure list of questions and answers.

blocks.content: Restate the offer with the concrete trial terms. New information, never a copy of the hero.

config.ctaLabel: match the page-wide CTA label verbatim

blocks.fallback: A tall closing section: one line, one button, one friction-reducing caption.

blocks.content: Grouped product, company, legal, status, and social links. Real destinations only.
blocks.fallback: A small-type footer with grouped links and a legal line.
